current_text.html: Every applicant for the ministry must put himself under the care of Presbytery, which should ordinarily be the Presbytery that has jurisdiction of the church of which he is a member. The endorsement of his Session must be given to the Presbytery, consisting of testimonials regarding his Christian character and promise of usefulness in the ministry. The endorsement should also describe the activities of ministry the applicant has participated in with brief evaluation. Every applicant for care shall be a member of the congregation whose session provides an endorsement for at least six months before filing his application, except in those cases deemed extraordinary by the Presbytery. Every applicant must file his application with the clerk of the Presbytery. An applicant for care may not be received under care and examined for ordination at the same meeting of the Presbytery, since he must serve a period of at least one year of internship prior to ordination (see BCO 19-7 and 21-4). An applicant for internship is obliged to be under care and may be licensed to preach the Gospel; further, one who is not already under care may be taken under care, be licensed to preach the Gospel, and become an intern at the same meeting of Presbytery.

relationships.title: Flexibility for candidates applying to come under presbytery care

metadata.summary: The CCB found the proposed amendment to BCO 18-2 allowing flexible application procedures for candidates not in conflict with the Constitution.

relationships.title: Six-month PCA membership requirement for ministerial candidacy from non-PCA church
relationships.disposition: advice given — BCO 18-2 probably requires PCA membership; overture recommended

metadata.summary: The CCB advised that BCO 18-2 probably requires PCA congregation membership for candidacy, but acknowledged varying presbytery practice and recommended an overture to clarify whether endorsement from a non-PCA ruling body is permissible.

relationships.title: Scope of the extraordinary clause for ordination candidates

metadata.summary: The CCB advised that under BCO 18-2 the extraordinary clause excuses only the six-month membership period, not the session endorsement, the two-month filing deadline, or the one-year internship sequence.

relationships.title: Prohibition of dual candidacy under BCO 18-7

metadata.summary: BCO 18-7 permits a candidate to retain home-church membership while under another presbytery's care, but does not allow simultaneous candidacy under two presbyteries.
